newsitem.title: MALDIVES: Pakistan "very cautious" ahead of talks with India.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan "very cautious" ahead of talks with India.

text.p: Pakistani Foreign Minister Gohar Ayub Khan on Saturday played down the prospects of a breakthrough in peace talks with India, saying there could be setbacks and negotiations would take a long time.

"Expectations should not be built up because unless the groundwork is there, there could be disappointments," Khan told reporters on the margins of a meeting of foreign ministers of the South Asian region.
Pakistani Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif and his Indian counterpart, Inder Kumar Gujral, were scheduled to hold their first face-to-face talks on Monday at a resort on this Indian Ocean island nation.

"Let's hope that something positive comes out, but one has to be very cautious on it. It will be a long, drawn-out negotiation. There will be no quick fix," said Khan, adding that a half-century-old quarrel over Kashmir was Pakistan's core issue.

"We have waited 50 years, there had been three wars," he said, referring to the three conflicts between the neighbouring countries since independence in 1947. Two out of the three wars were over the Kashmir region.
The talks between the two nations' leaders on Monday were to take place on the fringes of a summit of the seven-nation South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation (SAARC) in the Maldives.
